title.en: Orthonormal modal polynomial basis on the reference hypercube
title.zh: 参考超立方体上的正交归一模态多项式基

summary: Build a tensor or serendipity modal basis whose members are orthonormal under the unweighted inner product on [-1,1]^ndim, and evaluate, differentiate, reflect and project onto it.

identity.relation: integral over [-1,1]^ndim of b_i(z) b_j(z) dz = delta_ij
identity.direction: Declared basis family, dimension and polynomial order to a callable orthonormal member set
identity.definition: Members are products of one-dimensional orthonormal Legendre polynomials, one factor per reference axis, indexed by exponent tuples. The tensor family keeps every tuple in [0,order]^ndim; the serendipity family keeps only tuples where at most one axis has exponent two or greater, which removes the cost of a full tensor slot for cross terms that add no per-axis resolution. Members are ordered by total degree, then by descending exponent on the first axis, then the second, and so on. Quadrature is the tensor Gauss-Legendre rule of order+1 points per axis, which integrates every product of two members exactly.
identity.model: Modal polynomial discretization on a single reference hypercube
identity.geometry: Reference cell [-1,1]^ndim; no physical mesh or metric is implied
identity.coordinates: Logical coordinates z in [-1,1]^ndim, ascending along each axis
identity.boundary: No boundary condition is applied; the reference cell has no physical boundary
assumptions: Logical coordinates are converted to float64 and must be finite
A coefficient vector is only meaningful together with the family, dimension, order and member order that produced it

inputs.name: order
inputs.constraints: Non-negative integer; orders zero through three are qualified, higher orders are unqualified

outputs.name: basis
outputs.description: Basis handle exposing kind, ndim, order, num_basis, exponents(), evaluate, expand, gradient, flip_sign, quadrature and project
outputs.constraints: Members are orthonormal under the unweighted inner product on the reference cell

preconditions: Logical coordinates are finite and lie inside [-1,1]^ndim; the cell is the caller's reference cell, not a physical element
supported: Evaluating all members, an expansion, and one reference-coordinate derivative of an expansion
Reflecting an expansion across a reference axis by sign-flipping its odd powers
Projecting values sampled on the basis's own tensor Gauss rule back onto the members
The tested family, dimensions one through three and orders zero through three
excluded: No physical mesh, Jacobian, metric or cell measure is applied; mapping to a physical element is the caller's responsibility.
No boundary condition, upwinding, limiting or positivity handling is provided.
Serendipity members do not span the same polynomial space as the tensor family at the same order; the two are not interchangeable.
The projection is exact only for values sampled on this basis's own quadrature nodes.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError when kind is not tensor or serendipity, ndim is outside 1..6, order is negative or non-integral, a boolean is passed where an integer is required, coordinates are non-finite or outside the reference cell, a coordinate array has the wrong trailing axis, a coefficient or sample array has the wrong shape or contains a non-finite value, or a direction is outside range(ndim).
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Raises ValueError if the Gauss-Legendre root iteration does not converge; no approximate ordinates are substituted.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: The Gauss-Legendre Newton iteration is bounded at 200 sweeps per root and reports failure instead of returning an unconverged node.
failure_semantics.partial_results: Construction is atomic: a rejected basis exposes no members. Evaluation returns a complete array or raises; no partial member set is returned.

example.description: Build the two-dimensional second-order serendipity basis, confirm its eight members are orthonormal under its own Gauss rule, and check that projecting an expansion's own samples returns its coefficients.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.numerics.modal_basis import modal_basis

basis = modal_basis("serendipity", 2, 2)
assert basis.num_basis == 8

nodes, weights = basis.quadrature()
members = basis.evaluate(nodes)
gram = np.einsum("q,qi,qj->ij", weights, members, members)
coefficients = np.arange(8, dtype=float) - 3.5
recovered = basis.project(basis.expand(nodes, coefficients))
print("orthonormal within 1e-12:", bool(np.abs(gram - np.eye(8)).max() < 1e-12))
print("coefficients recovered within 1e-12:", bool(np.abs(recovered - coefficients).max() < 1e-12))
example.expected:
orthonormal within 1e-12: True
coefficients recovered within 1e-12: True

scope: Public callable signature and documented rejection behavior
Member counts and one-dimensional member literals against the reference kernel
Orthonormality, quadrature exactness and projection recovery on named fixtures
The executable example stored in this contract
verification.evidence_ceiling: Member-count agreement, orthonormality and projection recovery establish the documented relation on the tested family, dimension and order combinations; they do not establish convergence-order claims on a physical mesh, arbitrary-order tie-breaking, or agreement with any specific discretization package. Higher dimensions and orders outside the tested bounded set are unqualified.
known_limitations: Only dimensions one through six and orders zero through three are covered by the regression fixtures.
Serendipity member selection is exercised for orders zero through three only; higher orders are unqualified.
The projection is only exercised on the basis's own quadrature nodes, not on arbitrary sample locations.
The serendipity exponent rule is qualified only for orders zero through three; higher-order semantics are unqualified.
